case_name: Kamini Kumar Das Choudhury v State Of West Bengal & Ors
facts: The appellant was a Sub Inspector of Police serving in the Enforcement Branch of the Calcutta Police on 20th May 1951, when he was ordered by S. Mukherji, Deputy Commissioner of Police, to search a house at 13/2 Sir Guru Das Road, in Kankurgachi Basti.
He alleged that the search concluded at 6-30 a.m., and, thereafter, he had gone to take tea 'with the permission and/or knowledge of his immediate superior Sub Inspector S. N. Bose'.
The appellant was met by the Assistant Commissioner of Police, Ataur Rahman, when he was coming back, after taking tea, to the place of search.

He alleged that the Assistant Commissioner charged the appellant with dereliction of his duties, with disobedience of the order to remain at the post of his duty, with carrying out the search perfunctorily, with disloyalty and giving away of information of proposed searches to offending members of the public so that the purpose of the search, which was said to be detection of spurious ration cards, may be defeated.
The appellant was immediately suspended and the Assistant Commissioner Ataur Rahman was appointed the Enquiry Officer.
issues: Whether the Deputy Commissioner of Police had the power to dismiss the appellant from service
Whether there was a violation of Article 311 (1) of the Constitution
petitioner_arguments: The Deputy Commissioner of Police seemed to be of the same grade and status as the Principal of the Police Training School, Sharda, with the rank of a 'Superintendent', and who had appointed the appellant
There was no violation of Article 311 (1) of the Constitution
respondent_arguments: The Deputy Commissioner of Police did not have the power to dismiss the appellant from service
Article 311 (1) of the Constitution was violated
court_reasoning: The learned Single Judge thought it fit to consider and decide the point that the Deputy Commissioner of Police seemed to be of the same grade and status as the Principal of the Police Training School, Sharda, with the rank of a 'Superintendent', and who had appointed the appellant

The Division Bench observed that it appeared that the grounds raised against the proper conduct of the Enquiry and refusal of some of the prayers of the appellant made during its pendency were not pressed before the Trial Judge
holding: The appeal preferred by the appellant to the Inspector General of Police was also dismissed on 27-10-1951
The Division Bench dismissed the appeal principally on the ground of inordinate delay
